items.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

ctx.x: Because the rhythm section was older players?

They were older players, familiar with every standard in the Real Book and had been playing it for the millionth time. So here I come, young Sam, thinking I could, it just happened to everybody too. And then you had to be able to cut it, basically. So that was Wally’s experience. It’s like real life experience, getting punched in the face. And then © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
you’re like okay, I’d better go practice. I’d better go play this again if I ever set foot in there again. And then, you know, I just kept on playing in the Boston scene a lot.
